transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alicia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Tom Becker (Redwood SE), Maya Kline (Echelon Head of ML), Roberto Diaz (Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Security), Samir Patel (Product)

Summary:
Quick Optimize console walkthrough focused on prefetch + batching recommendations for a chat-heavy agent workload. Demoed cost-simulator scenarios (sessionized prefix cache vs stateless batching), discussed VPC/private deploy constraints, SOC2/KMS questions, and agreed on a short sandbox and baseline perf run. Customer is latency-sensitive but has tight cost targets for 10M monthly prompts.

Topics covered:
- Prefix/KV cache behavior for multi-turn agents
- Prefetch lookahead sizing and TTL tradeoffs
- Batch sizing and concurrency knobs in Redwood Console Optimize
- Cost-simulator assumptions (tokens, cache-hit rate, model variants)
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SAML/SSO, data retention

Action items (captured): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Nguyen: All right good afternoon everyone from Redwood, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — Tom and I will run through an Optimize walkthrough focused on prefetch and batching for the chat agents you described.
[00:18] Maya Kline: Hey thanks, excited. We've been worried about token spend and also latency spikes during peak. We run lots of short multi-turn sessions so curious about prefix caching.
[00:30] Tom Becker: Yep okay great. Quick outline: we'll open the console, show the Optimize tab, step through the cost simulator, then demo a couple of KV-prefetch profiles and how they interact with batching.
[01:02] Roberto Diaz: Quick governance note, we need details on VPC peering and whether we can run private control plane. Also our security team will ask about KMS and data-at-rest encryption.
[01:20] Alicia Nguyen: Absolutely — we'll include SOC 2 docs and the network diagram. We support both KMS and customer-managed HSM integrations for Private deployments.
[01:35] Priya Rao: When you say KMS, does that mean keys never leave customer control for the private model?
[01:45] Tom Becker: For Private you can bring your own KMS; for Hosted we can integrate with customer KMS via key wrapping and key policies. I'll share the security tech notes after the call.
[02:10] Samir Patel: Can we jump into the simulator? We can see the numbers with our traffic profile.
[02:20] Tom Becker: Sure, opening the Optimize console. (screen share) So here's the cost simulator. I've loaded a sample workload similar to what Maya shared: 9M monthly prompts, avg tokens/input 120, avg tokens/output 220, median session length 6 turns.
[02:48] Speaker 1: small stutter in the transcription here
[03:05] Tom Becker: Baseline: stateless batch, no prefetch, average latency 140ms p99 at 50 QPS. Cost estimate $24k/month using the L-affine model.
[03:30] Maya Kline: That baseline is roughly what we see in prod. Our spike windows double QPS for 10 minutes at a time.
[03:45] Tom Becker: Right, that's where prefetch + sessionization helps. Now, flip to the KV-prefetch profile. We'll configure a lookahead of 2 tokens — sorry, lookahead of 2 next-turn prefix tokens and TTL 12 hours for session cache.
[04:10] Roberto Diaz: Wait, TTL 12 hours seems long for us. How does TTL affect memory and cost?
[04:22] Tom Becker: Good question. TTL controls cache lifetime — longer TTL increases hit rate (so fewer model calls) but increases memory (KV cache size). The console shows estimated KV memory overhead and the projected hit-rate curve. For your traffic, a 12-hour TTL moved hit-rate from 28% to 46% in the sim.
[04:48] Maya Kline: That jump to 46% is impressive. What's the cost delta?
[04:55] Tom Becker: In this scenario tokens-per-month dropped by ~30% which lowers token bill to about $16.8k/month, but you add minimal infra costs for extra KV memory on Dedicated or Private hosts. Net savings still favorable.
[05:20] Priya Rao: Are there any PII exposures in prefix caching? We often have user identifiers in earlier turns.
[05:30] Alicia Nguyen: Prefix caching only stores model KV state — not raw user messages — but you can configure redaction or session-level encryption. For regulated data you can opt for Private and control retention policies.
[05:45] Priya Rao: Okay, want to review the retention API after this call.
[05:56] Tom Becker: Noted. Now demoing batching knobs: max_batch_size, max_latency_ms, and concurrency targets. If you set a slightly larger max_batch_size and a small concurrency cap, you can increase throughput while holding p99 below your 250ms SLO.
[06:20] Tom Becker: Example: increasing batch size from 8->16 improved tokens/sec by 1.6x but p99 increased from 140ms to 180ms; if we enable KV-prefetch the p99 drops back to 150ms because fewer full-model steps are needed.
[06:44] Maya Kline: So prefetch reduces model work per request and allows larger batch sizes without violating latency?
[06:51] Tom Becker: Exactly. Prefetch reduces average sequence length of full attention runs by keeping KV state for common prefixes.
[07:10] Samir Patel: Can you show the combined sim for dedicated capacity pricing? We have a Reserved budget that might make sense.
[07:22] Tom Becker: Sure — toggling to Dedicated pricing. For your 9M prompts pattern, Dedicated reserved instance with autoscale plus prefetch gives estimated infra commit of 3 nodes with burst capacity, and monthly platform fee — total around $19k/month compared to hosted $16.8k token-only, but with SLA and predictable throughput.
[07:48] Roberto Diaz: That $19k includes storage for KV cache?
[07:51] Tom Becker: It factors in a KV store estimate — we show memory and NVMe footprint. If you choose private on-prem shapes we'd need exact host sizing; Tom (SE) will run a baseline perf.
[08:10] Speaker 1: small audio overlap, someone clears throat
[08:28] Alicia Nguyen: Quick aside on routing: you can set a policy to route high-priority users to dedicated nodes, lower-priority to hosted to save cost. For mission-critical users, set fallback policies.
[08:42] Maya Kline: Interesting — we could route billing-critical flows to dedicated, others to hosted.
[08:50] Priya Rao: Does Redwood provide audit logs for every inference? We need per-request auditing.
[08:58] Tom Becker: Yes — audit logs include request metadata, model variant, latency, and costs at token granularity. For Private we can ship logs to your SIEM.
[09:18] Maya Kline: Can we look at cache eviction patterns? We have a lot of long-lived but low-volume sessions.
[09:28] Tom Becker: In console — cache heatmap. (shares) You can see TTL distribution and evictions. For your workload we noticed a tail of low-activity sessions; suggestion is to use a two-tier TTL: short TTL for anonymous sessions (30m) and long TTL for authenticated sessions (12h). That preserves cost savings while bounding memory.
[09:58] Samir Patel: The two-tier TTL makes sense. Any automated rules?
[10:05] Tom Becker: Yep you can add routing rules in the console based on user attributes. We'll include a sample policy in the sandbox.
[10:20] Maya Kline: Okay let's talk about prefetch sizing — how many steps to prefetch?
[10:28] Tom Becker: Common approach: lookahead of 1-3 tokens per turn for completion-heavy agents, and for multi-turn predictable flows you can prefetch next full-turn logits (lookahead 1 full-turn). In the sim: lookahead of 1 full-turn with TTL 6h produced 38% hit-rate and 24% token reduction.
[10:56] Roberto Diaz: Are there fragility concerns? If our user does path deviation, does prefetch make hallucinations worse?
[11:06] Tom Becker: Prefetch doesn't change model output semantics — it just caches KV states. If the user's next input diverges, cache will miss and we fallback to full-model. We recommend conservative prefetch and monitor perplexity/regression via Redwood Optimize eval hooks.
[11:30] Maya Kline: How does this interact with quantized model variants? We run q4 models in prod.
[11:36] Tom Becker: Redwood supports quantization-friendly runtimes. Cache semantics are identical. For some quantized kernels you'll see different perf curves — console sim has per-model performance profiles so you can toggle model variants (q4, int8, fp16) and see cost-latency tradeoffs.
[12:00] Alicia Nguyen: Quick Q from Sales: any competitor differentiation you want to call out?
[12:06] Tom Becker: Main diff is unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private plus the cost-simulator integrated with the console. Some vendors separate runtime from cost tooling which makes scenario planning laborious.
[12:20] Maya Kline: Could we import our real traffic CSV into the simulator?
[12:26] Tom Becker: Yes, upload CSV with timestamps/session ids/turn tokens. That gives an accurate sim. We'll accept your CSV for the sandbox.
[12:38] Speaker 1: small mislabel, says "Tom" but speaker was Maya
[12:50] Tom Becker: Next, quick demo of a live prefetch profile. I'm toggling ON prefetch for a canary population (5% of sessions). Watch the live trace: requests served from cache highlighted in green, full-model in orange.
[13:12] Maya Kline: I see the green hit markers. Are we able to measure regression in answer quality?
[13:20] Tom Becker: Yes console ties eval prompt sets to rollout. You can pin a prompt set — run before/after and get quality delta. We'll link an example eval for your agent flows.
[13:36] Samir Patel: If we see a quality regression can we rollback automatically?
[13:40] Alicia Nguyen: Yes — rollouts support automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts or latency breaches.
[13:50] Roberto Diaz: About peering and egress — do you support private connectivity across regions?
[13:58] Tom Becker: We do support cross-region VPC peering and regional fallbacks. If data residency requires regional-only models we can pin model placements.
[14:12] Priya Rao: On compliance: can we get the Data Processing Agreement and evidence of encryption in transit and at rest?
[14:20] Alicia Nguyen: We'll send SOC 2, DPA, and encryption docs in the follow-up. For Private you control KMS and logs.
[14:34] Maya Kline: Back to cost model — can you show a extreme-sensitivity sim? For example, if hit-rate drops by 10% what happens to monthly cost?
[14:45] Tom Becker: Toggling sensitivity: if hit-rate goes 46% -> 36% cost increases back to ~20.5k/month. Sensitivity table is in the sim UI; shows break-even points for commit size and hit-rate.
[15:05] Maya Kline: What's the recommended guardrail for p99 latency? We aim for p99 < 220ms.
[15:12] Tom Becker: We usually set concurrency caps + batch-size upper limit and enable prefetch; in the sim that reached p99 190ms. We'll include a recommended config.
[15:35] Alicia Nguyen: Quick note on observability: you'll get token-level cost breakdown per route, model, and token type (prompt/completion). Helpful to spot high-cost prompts.
[15:50] Maya Kline: Good, we have a few expensive system prompts to audit.
[16:00] Tom Becker: Final demo step: exporting the runbook. Console can auto-generate a playbook with suggested batch sizes, TTLs, and expected savings. I'm exporting and attaching to the session.
[16:20] Samir Patel: Perfect. For the sandbox, what should we prepare?
[16:25] Alicia Nguyen: Ideally: traffic CSV, a couple of prompt sets for eval, VPC peering contact, and a list of high-priority flows. We'll provision a 2-week sandbox with the cost-sim preloaded.
[16:40] Priya Rao: Security will want an inventory of data touched by the cache — does console show that?
[16:46] Tom Becker: We'll provide a data flow diagram and cache metadata — console shows what gets stored (KV IDs and size) but not raw PII payloads; we also support token-level redaction before caching.
[17:05] Maya Kline: One more thing — what's typical time to value for a pilot?
[17:12] Alicia Nguyen: From sandbox kickoff to measurable savings usually 2-3 weeks: one week for baseline and config, one week for canary and evaluation.
[17:25] Roberto Diaz: Anything else re: billing? If we test sandbox and it spikes usage, is that charged?
[17:32] Alicia Nguyen: Sandbox has rate limits and spend caps; production charges apply only once you move to live. We'll document the sandbox guardrails.
[17:45] Speaker 1: brief pause, typing sounds
[18:00] Tom Becker: Okay wrapping up — recap and next steps. We'll send: the cost-simulator CSV template, SOC 2/DPA, the exported playbook, and the recording. You'll provide: traffic CSV, VPC contact, and prompt sets.
[18:18] Maya Kline: Sounds good. Any blockers for security sign-off?
[18:25] Priya Rao: We'll need the DPA and an architectural diagram and confirmation of KMS model. After that we can greenlight a Private pilot.
[18:36] Alicia Nguyen: We'll include the architecture and KMS options in the follow-up.
[18:44] Samir Patel: Great, thanks — excited to see the sandbox numbers.
[18:49] Alicia Nguyen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the files and schedule the sandbox kickoff for next week.
[18:56] End of recorded transcript (note: transcription imperfect in spots; some speaker labels guessed)

Recap (short):
- Demoed cost-simulator with Echelon's traffic profile, showed prefetch + batching combos.
- Prefetch + TTL tuning expected to reduce token spend by ~20–30% in the modeled scenarios.
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs: predictability vs lower token-only price.
- Security questions noted; Redwood to share SOC2/DPA and KMS details.
- Next: sandbox (2 weeks), baseline perf run by Tom, and follow-ups with network/security docs.
